references.text: The cry of the children of Israel rose up to God because of their slavery, and God heard their groaning. This shows the background for God's word that their cry has reached him.
God confirms that he has heard the complaint of the children of Israel against the oppression of the Egyptians, and remembers his covenant.
Describes the oppression (לַחַץ) that the Egyptians inflicted on the Israelites through forced labor.
Moses reminds the people that they cried out to the Lord, and he heard their voice and saw their misery, toil, and oppression.
The Lord rises up because of the oppression of the poor and the groaning of the needy.
God looked upon them in their distress when he heard their cry.
Stephen quotes this verse and confirms that God saw his people's mistreatment in Egypt and heard their groaning.
The cry of the oppressed workers has reached the ears of the Lord of hosts, as an example that God hears the cry of the oppressed.
Exodus 2:23 describes the sequence of events (the cry for help rose up) which directly triggers God's response in Exodus 3:9.
